summary: NASA has revealed updated lunar lander timelines for SpaceX and Blue Origin alongside an Artemis III mission update, as SpaceX announced plans to attempt its first-ever double Starship rocket catch on its next test launch. In commercial space, SpaceX returned to profitability in the third quarter driven by satellite, computer leasing, and artificial intelligence revenues, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise prepares to launch an AI compute module to the moon aboard the FLIP rover and DARPA awarded Space Nuclear Power Corporation an agreement to ground-test an autonomous nuclear reactor controller. On the military front, U.S. Space Force officials are examining security implications after a Russian satellite engaged in close encounters with a U.S. commercial spacecraft likely used by Ukraine, while Congress requested answers regarding Starlink service disruptions in the region and a defense acquisition leader called for a third launch range by 2030. In civil space and science developments, NASA conducted an RS-25 engine test for future Artemis missions, deployed its CASALS instrument to fill gaps in Earth 3D mapping, and created experimental Mars helicopter blade designs for longer flight durations. Meanwhile, astronomers reexamining a Viking 2 signal identified a potential historic marsquake, and Hubble Space Telescope observations challenged established theories regarding the role of supernova winds in cosmic reionization. Skywatchers should look to the skies tonight for the peak of the annual Orionid meteor shower.
